v.rationale:
I ranked impl-3 first, impl-1 second and impl-2 third. All three tests pass (12, 12 and 13 tests).

**Shared across all three.** The code is nearly identical:
- The same #[Scope] inactiveFor, with whereNull OR last_login_at < now()->subDays()
- Commands defined with the #[Signature]/#[Description] attributes
- --days validated with filter_var
- The same Schedule::command()->dailyAt('06:00')->appendOutputTo() entry
- The same probes, run against all three: --days=0, '+5', ' 7 ', '1e2', '', a future last_login_at and very large day values

They all behave the same on those probes, except that impl-1 rejects 0. Very large values like PHP_INT_MAX make the date overflow and give a nonsense count in all three, so that doesn't separate them.

**Why impl-1 is not first.** It has the most thorough tests: it checks the timezone and output file in the schedule test, freezes time for every test and checks both sides of the boundary. But it hard-codes Europe/Copenhagen for the schedule. The task doesn't ask for that, and the app runs on UTC. A probe confirmed the job is not due at 06:00 app time, so I counted it as a small correctness issue. It also prints '1 users' and leaves a stray commented line in Pest.php.

**Why impl-2 is third.** It adds a useful index on the column. But the command prints only a bare number into an appended log file, which works against the goal of having the number show up in the logs. Its boundary test also checks only one side and doesn't assert success.

**Why impl-3 is first.** It is the cleanest and most proportionate: labelled output that makes sense in a log, a tidy Pest.php change, and good coverage including an empty-string --days and a test for the nullable column. Its only weak points are minor gaps in the tests.
